claims.claim: Amphilochius was a Christian bishop of Iconium in the fourth century.
Amphilochius was born perhaps at Caesarea around 339/340 and died probably between 394 and 403.
Amphilochius was made bishop of Iconium early in 374, probably placed there by Basil of Caesarea.
The work In illud: Pater si possibile est is a homily by Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, directed against heretics.
The homily addresses the words 'Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me' and responds to heretics who misunderstand this statement as indicating cowardice or weakness in Christ.
Most of Amphilochius' work has been lost, and only eight homilies have survived.
Amphilochius' style and concern for historical accuracy places him as a predecessor to John Chrysostom, who may have been influenced by him.
Amphilochius was regarded by his contemporaries as the foremost man in the Eastern church after Basil of Caesarea and Gregory of Nazianzus.
The works ascribed to Amphilochius are mostly spurious, and the Life is a later fiction.
